mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) below 1,500K units triggers a demand shock that depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1500 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate increase of at least 0.4 percentage points over three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >=0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production decline of more than 1% for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent surge in real savings deposits (RSAFS) above the 95th percentile for the past decade signals an abrupt policy easing and flight to safety, which compresses term premium and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND RSAFS > 95th percentile for 10 years
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals improving household purchasing power, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate above 6% and a fall in average hourly earnings (implied by PAYEMS and UNRATE interaction) signals a wage-price decoupling, which reduces inflationary pressure and increases the likelihood of rate cuts, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production above 0.8% for six consecutive months signals a robust supply expansion, which improves corporate earnings and reduces input costs, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained INDPRO growth above 0.8% (t-test p > 0.05).
